title: Formalisme algébrique des correspondances et algèbres de Poincaré-Hodge (cf conjectures standard) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), lettres (1966-1967).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the earlier pages of this manuscript. E is a graded k-algebra of 'correspondences' acting on a graded module M = ⊕_{i=0}^{2n} M^i, in the abstract model of cohomology of a smooth projective variety of dimension n. The π_i are the Künneth projectors: mutually orthogonal idempotents summing to 1. E^0, the degree-0 part, is the commutant of the π_i, so the π_i lie in the centre Z(E^0), which is commutative. ξ^{2n-i}_i = π_{2n-i} E π_i denotes the correspondences of degree 2n-2i sending M^i to M^{2n-i}; the model is the Lefschetz operator L^{n-i}.

The question is the uniqueness of the π_i. Induction from the previous page: suppose the π_α for α outside [i, 2n-i] are known, with i < n-1. Then φ_i = Σ_{α≥i} π_α and ψ_{2n-i} = Σ_{α≤2n-i} π_α are known. Hence ψ_{2n-i} E^{2n-2i} φ_i = π_{2n-i} E π_i = ξ^{2n-i}_i is known, even before π_i and π_{2n-i} are.

This page states the conditions that pin down π_i and π_{2n-i}:
- (3.1)_i: if u ∈ Z(E^0) and ξ^{2n-i}_i u = 0, then π_i u = 0.
- (3.2)_i: if u ∈ Z(E^0) and u ξ^{2n-i}_i = 0, then π_{2n-i} u = 0.

Why this suffices. Since u commutes with π_i, vu = vπ_i u for every v ∈ ξ^{2n-i}_i, so the reverse implication is automatic. Thus (3.1)_i says exactly that Ann_{Z(E^0)}(π_i) equals the left annihilator in Z(E^0) of the already-known set ξ^{2n-i}_i. In a commutative ring an idempotent is determined by its annihilator: Ann(e) = (1-e)Z, and if Ann(e) = Ann(f) then e = ef = f. Hence π_i is determined, and likewise π_{2n-i} by (3.2)_i. Induction on i, closed at the middle by π_n = 1 - Σ_{α≠n} π_α, determines all π_i. So under (3.1)_i and (3.2)_i for all i, the Künneth grading is unique and is determined by the ring structure alone.

Section 4 gives sufficient conditions when E acts on M as in §1 (faithfully, inside End M):
- (4.1)_i: the kernels of the v : M^i → M^{2n-i}, v ∈ ξ^{2n-i}_i, have zero intersection. Then ξu = 0 forces the image of u|_{M^i} into that intersection, so π_i u = 0; this gives (3.1)_i.
- (4.2)_i: the images of these v span M^{2n-i}. Dually this gives (3.2)_i.
- (4.3)_i: some v ∈ ξ^{2n-i}_i is an isomorphism M^i → M^{2n-i}. This hard-Lefschetz-type condition implies both (4.1)_i and (4.2)_i.

The page breaks off there. Purpose: an abstract, ring-theoretic proof that a Lefschetz-type axiom (standard conjecture B, or the weaker joint injectivity/surjectivity) forces uniqueness of the Künneth decomposition inside the algebra of correspondences. This belongs to the 'Poincaré–Hodge algebra' axiomatics for the standard conjectures.
errors: No mathematical error found. The annihilator argument is correct because π_i and u lie in the commutative ring Z(E^0).
The inductive step as written covers i < n-1; the case i = n-1 is handled on the previous page. The base case (i = 0, using π_α = 0 outside [0,2n]) is implicit.
The passage (4.1)⇒(3.1) needs E to act faithfully on M, so that π_i u = 0 iff u|_{M^i} = 0. This is presumably what 'comme dans 1.' supplies but it is not restated.
Minor slip: the line about (4.1)_i is written twice in the manuscript.

ideas.what: Künneth projectors as central idempotents of the degree-0 commutant, each determined by its annihilator in Z(E^0).
ideas.modern_name: uniqueness of (homological) Künneth decomposition; idempotents in commutative rings determined by annihilators
ideas.usually_credited_to: Künneth standard conjecture C: Grothendieck (1968, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles'), Kleiman (1968)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Standard conjectures on algebraic cycles' (Bombay 1968) states C and B but not, to my knowledge, this abstract uniqueness argument

ideas.what: Inductive determination of π_i, π_{2n-i} from the outer projectors via ξ^{2n-i}_i = ψ_{2n-i} E φ_i, under a Lefschetz-type non-degeneracy condition.
ideas.modern_name: Lefschetz standard conjecture B implies Künneth uniqueness/algebraicity
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck; Kleiman, 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' (1968), where C is derived from B via L and Λ
ideas.where_published: related statements in Grothendieck 1968 and Kleiman 1968/1994; this exact proof is unsure

ideas.what: Weakening of hard Lefschetz to joint injectivity (4.1) and joint surjectivity (4.2) of the whole space of correspondences M^i → M^{2n-i}.
ideas.modern_name: weak form of Lefschetz-type condition (family version of B)

missed.claim: An abstract criterion for uniqueness of a Künneth grading inside an algebra of correspondences. The required non-degeneracy is only that the family of all correspondences M^i → M^{2n-i} be jointly injective and jointly surjective, which is weaker than a single Lefschetz isomorphism. It is phrased purely ring-theoretically, through annihilators in Z(E^0).
missed.quote: L'intersection des noyaux des v : M^i → M^{2n-i}, pour v ∈ ξ_i^{2n-i}, est réduite à 0.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Abstract 'Künneth-type gradings' of correspondence algebras occur in Chow–Künneth decompositions (Murre), in the motivic Lefschetz literature, and in uniqueness questions for gradings of motives. A purely algebraic uniqueness criterion weaker than hard Lefschetz could be of mild interest. It is likely folklore or easily rederived.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but elementary argument within Grothendieck's unpublished Poincaré–Hodge axiomatics, a weak form of the known principle that Lefschetz-type conditions control the Künneth components. The only mildly notable detail is the weakening to jointly injective/surjective families, which I cannot confirm is in print.
transcription_corrections: 'Lorsque ξ* est commutatif [?] ou (3.2)_i 1.' should read roughly 'Lorsque E est comme dans 1., une condition suffisante pour avoir (3.1)_i et (3.2)_i est la suivante'. The marginal '(3.2)_i' belongs with '(3.1)_i' below it, and the word is 'comme', not 'commutatif'.
'Zξ^0' is Z(E^0), the centre of E^0; the symbols ξ and E denote the same calligraphic E (correspondence algebra).
First line: 'u_{2n-i}' is probably 'π_{2n-i}' (continuing 'l'unicité de π_i, π_{2n-i}'), followed by '...sont les conjonctions des [conditions] suivantes'.
'donnent une procédé [?] pour déterminer en fonction [?] des [?] π_i' likely reads 'donnent un procédé ... pour déterminer de proche en proche les π_i'.
'Ces deux conditions ... et satisfaites [?] lorsque [?]' should read 'Ces deux conditions (sur v : M^i → M^{2n-i}) sont satisfaites si'.
